newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds flat, await retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds flat, await retail sales data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds were modestly mixed on Wednesday as market participants saw little opportunity to take any firm positions, mortgage experts said.
With little supply to satisfy demand pass-throughs have been trading in a very narrow range, they said.
"(Mortgages) are trading at such tight levels over Treasuries, it is difficult to get anything done in here with the lack of supply," said one pass-through trader.
At 1600 EDT/2000 GMT Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were even at 100-03/32 bid, yielding 99 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was unchanged at 100-03/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues were up 1/32 at 100-08/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.45 percent, while the 10-year T-note was up 3/32 to yield 6.56 percent.

Cynthia Rivera, a mortgage research analyst at BZW Securities Inc, said that mortgages are expected to continue to trade within a narrow range until the Treasury market takes enough direction to force them out.
Portfolio managers have yet to dump their pass-through holdings, despite the current tight levels, said Rivera.
"There is no danger," she said. Investors may even stomach a couple of basis points of widening, she said.
Market players said they may get some direction if the Commerce Department's retail sales report surprises Wall Street expectations.

On average, economists in a Reuters poll forecast retail sales rose 0.4 percent in May versus a 0.3 percent decline in April. Excluding autos, the experts projected retail sales increased 0.3 percent from a 0.1-percent drop.
